body.estimand_functional: If \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) satisfies the query-local first-jet-determining and latent-separator-relative fibre-coherence assumptions and \((\widehat G,\mathcal T)=\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X})\), then \(\theta_G=[\widehat G]\).  Outside that strict subclass, RankPeel is only a partial oracle-relative procedure and no identifying equality is asserted.

sampling_model.design: Population observational identification; there is no intervention or randomization design.
sampling_model.units: One scalar random vector indexed by the finite layered vertex set, with only \(X\) observed.
sampling_model.treatment: None; the target is the causal structure rather than a treatment effect.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None in the population theorem.  The partial functional \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}\) is determined by the observed law on \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), and oracle evaluation cost is excluded from query complexity.  Structural recovery additionally assumes query-local first-jet determinacy and latent-separator-relative fibre coherence; the latter is not an observable nuisance condition.

body.tldr: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang already identify the full binary adjacency matrix of their nonlinear latent hierarchy and already reuse measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates.  RankPeel is a deterministic population protocol whose pair tests and canonical parent-deletion tests use at most \(p^2+p\) combined observed-law queries and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping.  The unchanged published Conditions 1--3 are not enough for that law-invariant protocol: the smooth boundary member \(X_1=\cdots=X_4=H\) admits conditional-mean versions with different transverse Jacobian ranks.  Exact reconstruction is proved instead on the strict subclass where the predictor supports of queries actually requested by canonical RankPeel are first-jet determining and the particular latent separator cuts used by those queries have fibre-coherent conditional versions.  Fibre coherence is latent and separator-relative, not observable.  The exact \(k\)-versus-\(k+1\) neutrality theorem covers only the least-labelled representatives and candidate states actually evaluated by that canonical execution; replay remains an oracle-relative corollary.

project_justification.gap: The closest nonlinear result already identifies the complete binary adjacency matrix and already uses measured pure descendants recursively, but its construction exhaustively searches subset families and gives no explicit polynomial observed-query budget.  Its Conditions 1--3 also do not make every pointwise conditional-mean Jacobian rank an observed-law functional: on lower-dimensional predictor support, smooth versions can agree almost surely while having different transverse derivatives.
project_justification.niche: A deterministic pairwise and canonical-deletion protocol gives a quadratic population query schedule, but exact structural recovery is honest only on the strict query-local subclass where actual predictor supports determine first jets and the actual latent separator cuts admit fibre-coherent versions.
project_justification.fill: The repaired contribution proves the restricted separator bound under those two explicit query-local hypotheses, exact canonical execution-local neutrality, recursive adjacency recovery on that subclass, an unconditional \(p^2+p\) execution budget, and an oracle-relative replay record with conditional structural soundness.  It preserves the published-class counterexample and makes no unchanged-class strict-tightening claim.

body.related_work: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang identify the full binary adjacency matrix up to latent permutation and use measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates.  RankPeel changes the construction to deterministic pair tests and canonical parent deletion and proves a quadratic oracle budget, but its recovery theorem requires additional query-local first-jet determinacy and latent-separator-relative fibre coherence, so it is not an unchanged-class strict tightening.  Huang, Low, Xie, Glymour, and Zhang inform the pure-descendant surrogate motif in a linear IL\(^{2}\)H model, but their covariance-rank assumptions and Markov-equivalence target differ.  Kong, Huang, Xie, Xing, Chi, and Zhang identify nonlinear latent representations only up to invertible transformations rather than through this observed conditional-mean rank protocol.  Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma motivate the separation between graph-forced rank upper bounds and generic path-based lower bounds in the linear Gaussian case.  Hatcher's invariance-of-domain theorem and Rudin's inverse-function theorem support the topological bottleneck argument; neither source supplies the causal query-regularity assumptions.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The prescribed early-kill audit covered all \(676\) stated three-level graphs and all \(60{,}892\) enumerated level-zero and retained-surrogate cuts without a d-separation counterexample, but finite enumeration is not the recursive graphical proof.  Analytically, the unchanged published Conditions 1--3 fail to determine Jacobian rank across conditional-mean versions: the explicit smooth boundary model \(X_1=\cdots=X_4=H\) yields valid pair representatives of ranks one and two.  The recovery theorem therefore assumes first-jet determinacy only on predictor sets actually requested and fibre coherence only for the latent separators actually used.  Fibre coherence is not observable from \(P_X\).  No blanket separator-equals-rank identity, extra saturated-rank condition, faithfulness inheritance after contraction, finite-sample Jacobian rate, or image-data consistency is asserted.
body.honest_scope: The causal target remains the full layered adjacency matrix modulo within-layer latent permutations.  The proved identifying map is RankPeel only on the strict subclass of published models satisfying query-local first-jet determinacy and latent-separator-relative fibre coherence along the canonical execution.  The unchanged class contains the explicit equal-measurement boundary model on which RankPeel requests a version-unstable pair and returns \(\bot\), so completeness and exact recovery are not claimed there.  The \(p^2+p\) call count, \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping bound, and replay completeness are unconditional properties of the partial oracle procedure; structural soundness of the returned graph is conditional on the strict-subclass hypotheses.  Alternate representatives, alternate deletion orders, counterfactual candidate states, oracle evaluation time, nonparametric estimation, finite-sample recovery, and CelebA consistency are outside scope.
body.interpretation: On the strict query-regular subclass, equality of the canonical baseline and augmented ranks certifies that the currently tested candidate set contains every parent of the processed mixed child.  A failed equality identifies the omitted candidate as indispensable at that canonical deletion step.  The transcript certifies deterministic consistency with the same population oracle, not the unobserved fibre-coherence condition or the unchanged published model class.
